Subject: Dedicated pool qualification — discovery recap & next steps

Hi Alice / Bob,

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we stay aligned. I tried to keep this tight — if I missed anything call it out and I’ll update.

Pain points you called out
- 99th percentile latency spikes during morning batch jobs affect downstream analytics dashboards.
- Current self-hosted setup (in-house GPUs + spun-up cloud instances) is unpredictable and operationally heavy.
- Regulatory requirement: subsets of customer data must be isolated per-contract (legal/regulatory ask).
- Need predictable throughput for embedding generation (rough target ~120–150 requests/sec under steady state).

Success criteria you described
- p99 inference latency predictable and under target for interactive inference (goal: p99 token generation latency within acceptable SLO; we captured 200–300ms target range during discussion).
- Reserve capacity that guarantees isolation for regulated customers and avoids noisy neighbor issues.
- Autoscaling/burst policy that can absorb short periodic spikes without manual ops.
- Integration with your audit/logging pipeline (SOC2 evidence + access to request-level logs).

What we proposed (high-level)
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) with tenant isolation per-pool and optional VPC peering.
- Starter pool recommendation: 2–4 GPUs (A100/80GB equiv) for initial pilot; scale to N pools for production traffic. Exact sizing depends on model choice/quantization — see attached dedicated-sizing.xlsx.
- Burst policy: pre-warmed buffer + short-term burst with automatic fallback to smaller model variant.
- Observability: token-level latency and per-route dashboards in Redwood Console, plus exportable logs for audits.

Immediate next steps
1) Technical deep-dive with Rishi and Monica (target Thu, 5/22, 10:00am PT) — go/no-go on pooling config and confirm model/quantization options.
2) We will circulate a first-pass mutual action plan / MOA and a draft SOW for procurement.
3) Security questionnaire: Monica will share SOC2 evidence checklist and logging export sample.
4) Pilot timeline: tentative 6-week pilot (pilot sizing and goals to be defined in deep-dive).

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-overview.pdf, dedicated-sizing.xlsx

Thanks — I’ll send a calendar invite for Thursday and Rishi will lead the technical portion.

Best,

Thanks Alice — quick answers ahead of the deep-dive and a few technical notes so we can use the meeting efficiently.

Billing model (short):
- Reserved capacity: monthly commitment for the pool (GPU-hour equivalent) + base rate.
- Burst: typically metered as overage on a per-GPU-hour basis for reserved pools, or per-token billing if using hosted fallback. We can provide a blended estimate in the SOW depending on expected burst characteristics.

Pool behavior and onboarding (short):
- Pre-warmed slots are exclusive to the pool by default (ensures isolation). We also support account-level shared burst buffers as an opt-in to reduce committed capacity.
- Onboarding for a staging canary: ~2 business days to provision networking + pool + test credentials (assuming VPC peering is in place). If you need an on-prem proof-of-concept it’s a longer cadence.

Sizing note (assumptions):
- For your 130 req/s steady-state embedding target, a 4x A100-80GB equivalent pool running efficient batching and int8 quantization (if model supports it) is likely to meet throughput with good latency headroom. Actual numbers depend on model, max sequence length, and batching window. See attached moa-draft.docx for the MOA skeleton and a quick expected throughput table.

Data & compliance
- We support configurable log exports (S3/Cloud Storage) with retention policies, plus per-request IDs for traceability. Monica will follow up with the SOC2 artifact list and an example log export.

I’ll take the deep-dive on model and runtime tuning on Thu. Looking forward to walking through a live trace and sizing.

Thanks,
